questions.stem: What does the man say about the weekly program?
questions.stemZh: 男士对这个每周节目有何评价?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Welcome to Money Matters, a weekly program that helps you manage your money. Tonight, I'll be talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting. 欢迎收听《金钱要事》，这是一档帮你管理钱财的每周节目。今晚，我将和玛丽·约翰逊聊聊 预算的话题。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 开场点题句。节目开头的自我介绍 a weekly program that helps you manage your money 加上 talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting，是典型的"开场点题"信号—— 节目类录音常在第一两句报出自己是干嘛的，这句就是定位锚。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting ↔helps people with budgeting 原词budgeting+功能补全

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 录音说节目"helps you manage your money"（帮你管钱），不是帮你"earn more money"（赚更多钱）；管钱 ≠ 赚钱，方向被偷换。 借用原文：helps you manage your money B) 未提及 录音谈的是 budgeting（预算/记账），并没说节目"teaches the importance of financing"（讲融资/理财的重要性）；financing 与 budgeting 是相近理财词，盗用相近 概念来诱选，原文未提"重要性"这一说法。 D) 原词陷阱 选项 introduces a novel way to invest 借"理财"氛围里的 invest 来诱选，但录音全程讲预 算与记账，从未介绍"新的投资方式"，是听到理财就联想投资的陷阱。

options.label: B

options.label: D

questions.stem: What did the man read recently?
questions.stemZh: 男士最近读到了什么?
questions.answerText: Most Americans do not stick to a budget.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: That's easier said than done. I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget. 说起来容易做起来难。我最近读到，只有 41% 的美国人会坚持执行预算。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: I read recently 引出句。I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget 由"I read recently that…"直接引出"读到的内容"，是答案句的明确信号——"读到 了什么"的答案就跟在该信号之后。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget ↔Most Americans do not stick to a budget. 肯否转换+量词换算

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 录音这处只说"坚持预算的比例低"，没提美国人"not satisfied with their income"（对收入 不满）；满意度是另起的话题，原文未涉及。 B) 原词陷阱 no idea about how to invest 借理财氛围里的 invest 诱选，但这句数据讲的是"坚持预 算"，与"会不会投资"无关，是听到理财词就联想的陷阱。 C) 偷换概念 do not know how to save money 把原文的"坚持预算（budget）"偷换成"不会存钱 （save）"；后文虽另有 most people have no idea how much they spend，但那是"不 清楚花了多少"，不等于"不会存钱"，且本题要的是"读到的那条"，对应的是 41% 那句。 借用原文：adhere to a budget

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest the man do first to avoid getting into debt?
questions.stemZh: 女士建议男士首先做什么来避免负债?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Well, it's all about keeping track of your money. If you don't do that, you'll never be able to set any goals for your budget or have the discipline to stick to them. 嗯，关键全在于记录你的钱。如果你不这么做，就永远没法为预算设定目标，也没有自律去 坚持它们。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: it's all about 强调首要。it's all about keeping track of your money 用"it's all about…"强调"一切的根本在于"，是把某动作点为"首要/第一步"的信号；后接 If you don't do that… 进一步坐实它是前提，故这是"先做什么"的答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: keeping track of your money ↔Keep track of his money. near原词+人称转换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 答非所问 Live within his means. 对应原文 If the result is positive, you are living within your means.，那是"记账并做收支相减之后"才谈到的结果，不是题目要的"first（第一步）"；盗 用 living within your means 原词，却答非"先做什么"。 借用原文：living within your means C) 原词陷阱 Find more sources of income. 沾原文 adding up all of your sources of income 与 find yourself a part-time job 的边，但"找更多收入来源"在录音里是 Failing that（实在不行） 的最后一招，绝非"第一步"。 借用原文：sources of income D) 答非所问 Refrain from buying luxuries. 对应原文 cutting back on those non-essential items， 属"算出是负数后"要做的调整，同样不是"第一步"；它答非题目限定的 first。 借用原文：cutting back on those non-essential items

questions.stem: What does the woman say about online shopping?
questions.stemZh: 女士对网上购物有何评价?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Try cutting back on those non-essential items, sell some stuff in your attic, or shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate. 试着削减那些非必需品，把阁楼里的一些东西卖掉，或者网上购物以避开像巧克力那样不必 要的诱惑。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: shop online to avoid 目的状语。shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations 里 to avoid 是"网购为了避开…"的目的状语，直接点出网购的好处所在，是本题答案信号——好 处就藏在 to 后面那一段。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate ↔ It helps avoid unnecessary spending. 诱惑 花销的概括等值

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 录音只说网购能"避开诱惑"，没说它 offers a greater variety of items（商品更多 样）；"商品多"是网购的生活常识，但本句原文没这么说。 C) 过度推断 It changes one's way of living. 把"避开一次诱惑"夸成"改变生活方式"，原文 shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations 远没到"改变生活方式"的程度，是过度拔高。 D) 原词陷阱 It saves one's time for shopping. 借"shopping"原词与网购"省时"的常识诱选，但录音说 的是"避开诱惑"，从未提网购"省时间"，是听到 shop/online 就联想常识的陷阱。 借用原文：shop online 1 M: Hi there, I've come to see the flat. My name is Mark Adams. We spoke on the phone on Wednesday. M: 你好，我是来看公寓的。我叫Mark Adams。我们周三在电话里聊过。 2 W: Hi, Mark, come on up. I'll buzz you in. Green door on the second floor on the right side. Nice to meet you, I spoke to all your references and they all checked out okay. So let me show you around. The place actually belongs to my mother, but her health isn't great, so we finally managed to persuade her to move in with us and rent this old place out. W: 嗨，Mark，上来吧。我给你开门。二楼右边的绿色门。很高兴见到你，我联系了你所有的推荐人，他 们都没问题。那我带你四处看看。这房子其实是我妈妈的，但她身体不太好，所以我们终于说服她搬来和 我们一起住，把这老房子租出去。 3 M: It's a great size. Plenty of space. Very versatile. I think it's a winner for us. M: 面积很大。空间充足。非常实用。我觉得我们选它没错。 4 W: Yes, all the appliances are brand-new. There's a washing machine and a tumble dryer in the utility room next to the kitchen. W: 是的，所有电器都是全新的。厨房旁边的杂物间里有洗衣机和烘干机。 5 M: Lots of closet space too, which is fabulous. My wife has a ridiculous number of shoes. Now, the big question: What about noise and the neighbours? M: 储物空间也很多，太棒了。我妻子的鞋多得离谱。现在，最重要的问题：噪音和邻居情况怎么样？ 6 W: Well, all the neighbours are elderly, so no noisy kids. And the back of the house overlooks a clear and peaceful pond, so it's perfect if tranquility is what you are looking for. W: 嗯，所有邻居都上了年纪，所以没有吵闹的孩子。房子后面对着一个清澈宁静的池塘，所以如果你想 要的是安静，这里很完美。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 7 M: That's good news. We've been living in a less than glamorous part of Aberdeen, constantly harassed day and night by noisy neighbours. Getting to work was a nightmare too, as we only have one car and my wife has to use it as she works nights at the hospital. M: 那是好消息。我们一直住在Aberdeen一个不怎么样的地方，日夜不停地被吵闹的邻居骚扰。上班也是 个噩梦，因为我们只有一辆车，我妻子得用，她在医院上夜班。 8 W: Well, if you like the place, it's yours, as soon as I get a contract drawn up with the solicitor. The first month's rent and a deposit are mandatory on signing the contract. Then we can work out when is the best day for you to pay rent each month. W: 嗯，如果你喜欢这房子，它就是你的了，等我找律师把合同拟好。签合同时必须付第一个月的租金和 押金。然后我们可以商量每个月哪天交租对你最方便。 9 M: We'll be incredibly happy to be your new tenants. Thank you so much, My wife will be thrilled to get out of the shabby place we are now in, and start filling those wardrobes with all those shoes. M: 我们会非常高兴成为你的新租客。非常感谢，我妻子能搬出我们现在住的破地方，开始把那些衣柜装 满她所有的鞋子，她会兴奋坏了。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: mandatory 标出强制动作，触发条件 on signing 对齐。答案句靠强制信号定位：are mandatory on signing the contract中 mandatory（必须的）直接点出强制要求，且 on signing the contract 与题干触发条件逐字对齐，落点无疑。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: The first month's rent and a deposit are mandatory ↔Pay the first month's rent and a deposit 名词"是必须的"改写成动词"去支付"

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 Talk to his wife about the contract terms借了 contract 一词，可录音里男方提妻子是说 她上班用车、鞋多，从没说签约时要"和妻子商量合同条款"；听到 contract 就选，正中原 词陷阱。 借用原文：as soon as I get a contract drawn up C) 张冠李戴 Check the references of the flat owner盗用 references，但原文是女方说 I spoke to all your references and they all checked out okay——查证明人的是房东、查的是租客；选 项把施受方整个调反，且与"签约时"无关。 借用原文：I spoke to all your references and they all checked out okay D) 张冠李戴 Consult his solicitor one more time借走 solicitor，可原文是女方说 as soon as I get a contract drawn up with the solicitor——找律师拟合同的是女方；"男方再咨询一次律 师"原文并无，张冠李戴。 借用原文：as soon as I get a contract drawn up with the solicitor

questions.stem: Why does the man say his wife will feel very excited if they move into the flat?
questions.stemZh: 为什么男士说如果他们搬进这套公寓,他的妻子会非常兴奋?
questions.answerText: She will have plenty of space for her shoes.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: My wife will be thrilled to get out of the shabby place we are now in, and start filling those wardrobes with all those shoes. 我妻子一定会兴奋极了，能搬出我们现在这破地方，开始把那些衣柜塞满她所有的鞋子。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: wife 被点名 + thrilled，兴奋理由紧贴其后。答案句靠"本人被点名 + 情绪词"定位：My wife will be thrilled里 thrilled 正对题干 very excited，其后紧跟的 filling those wardrobes with all those shoes就是兴奋的具体理由——衣柜能装下她所有鞋。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: filling those wardrobes with all those shoes ↔She will have plenty of space for her shoes "衣柜塞满鞋"概括为"有足够地方放鞋" Lots of closet space too, which is fabulous. My wife has a ridiculous number of shoes ↔ She will have plenty of space for her shoes 前文 closet space + 鞋多，提前埋下"放鞋空间"伏笔

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 She can have a wonderful view of the pond借走原词 pond，录音确有 overlooks a clear and peaceful pond，但那是女方介绍房况，男方说妻子兴奋时绑的是鞋、不是池 塘；听到 pond 就选，正中原词陷阱。 借用原文：overlooks a clear and peaceful pond B) 过度推断 She will be much closer to her work place能从 she works nights at the hospital、上班 难联想，但原文只说现住处通勤是噩梦，并没说搬进新房"离单位更近"或妻子为此兴奋，属 过度推断。 借用原文：she works nights at the hospital C) 未提及 She can make friends with new neighbours借了 neighbours，可原文 all the neighbours are elderly只说邻居都上了年纪、不吵，从没说妻子会"和新邻居交朋友"，纯 属添加。 借用原文：all the neighbours are elderly Section B 1 A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels. Why? Because the more television kids watch, the more they're exposed to advertising. The more advertising they see, the more likely they are to insist on purchasing items when they go with their parents to the store. This could generate conflict if the parents refuse. All that, researchers say, can contribute to parents' overall stress levels. 一项新研究发现,儿童看电视的时间与其父母的压力水平之间存在正相关关系。为什么?因为孩子们看电视 越多,接触到的广告就越多。他们看到的广告越多,在与父母去商店购物时就越有可能坚持要购买商品。如 果父母拒绝,这可能会产生冲突。研究人员表示,所有这些都会加剧父母的整体压力水平。 2 What's the solution? Perhaps the most obvious is curtailing screen time. Commercial content is there for a reason: to elicit purchasing behavior. So parents might want to shut off the TV. Researchers concede that this is easier said than done. So they suggest another option. Parents can change how they talk to their kids about purchases. 解决方案是什么?也许最显而易见的是减少屏幕时间。商业内容的存在是有原因的:引发购买行为。因此父 母可能想要关闭电视。研究人员承认这说起来容易做起来难。所以他们提出了另一个选择。父母可以改变 与孩子谈论购物的方式。 Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. 3 The researchers suggest that parents seek input from their children on family purchasing decisions. They shouldn't try to control all purchases. Instead, parents might tell their children things like "I will listen to your advice on certain products or brands." This type of communication, the researchers assert, can lead to children making fewer purchasing demands. That means less parents' stress. 研究人员建议父母在家庭购买决策中征求孩子的意见。他们不应试图控制所有购买行为。相反,父母可以告 诉孩子诸如"在某些产品或品牌上我会听取你的建议"之类的话。研究人员断言,这种类型的沟通可以让孩子 减少购买要求。这意味着父母的压力会减少。 4 However, the protective effect of this kind of communication diminishes with greater exposure to television. This is because advertising aimed at children is especially persuasive. Advertisers use an assortment of tactics, such as bright colors, happy music and celebrity endorsements to appeal to children. Plus, children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent. analysis.text: B) 张冠李戴 「得不到应有回报」呼应录音前文 reward good people 的奖励话题，但那是开头铺垫，并 非第 4 段 discourage 的诱因；把别段的内容安到本题头上。 借用原文：we do indeed reward good people C) 未提及 「不得不做太多牺牲」录音通篇没提 sacrifice，是对行善代价的常识联想；录音说的打击是 被斥伪善，不是牺牲过多。 D) 偷换概念 「被周围人误解」听着像 dismissed as hypocritical，但「误解」是中性的认知偏差，录音 说的是被恶意贬斥为伪善，程度与性质都不同，属把「被斥伪善」悄悄换成更轻的「被误 解」。 借用原文：dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds Section C 1 In America, most researchers concede that boys and girls are brought up in different ways, taught different skills and rewarded for different acts. Women, it is agreed, excel at certain tasks, men at others. There's little argument that some personality traits appear more dominant in one sex than in the other. All of this notwithstanding, gender differences are very much in the media these days. Since the rise of the women's movement, gender role behavior has come under closer scrutiny. How has this affected friendship? How do the sexes differ in their friendship relations? 在美国,大多数研究者承认男孩和女孩以不同的方式被抚养,被教授不同的技能,并因不同的行为而获得奖 励。人们一致认为,女性擅长某些任务,男性擅长另一些任务。某些人格特质在一种性别中比另一种性别更 Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. 占主导地位,这一点几乎没有争议。尽管如此,性别差异如今在媒体中备受关注。自女性运动兴起以来,性别 角色行为受到了更严格的审视。这如何影响了友谊?两性在友谊关系上有何不同? 2 Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age. Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships; they do not differ in this respect. However, the type of play engaged in during these early friendships is telling of the difference to come. Boys tend to form play groups that are competitive in nature; girls' groups more frequently revolve around cooperative enterprises. Thus, at an early age, boys become concerned with trying hard and winning while girls, by contrast, play house and school, engaging in roles that require complementary support. 大多数青春期前的儿童都有一个最好的朋友,通常是同性别且年龄相仿的人。两性对这些童年友谊都有本质 上积极的回忆,在这方面他们并无差异。然而,这些早期友谊中参与的游戏类型预示了未来的差异。男孩倾 向于形成具有竞争性质的游戏群体,而女孩的群体更频繁地围绕合作性活动展开。因此,在很小的年纪,男孩 就开始关注努力尝试和获胜,而相比之下,女孩玩过家家和学校游戏,扮演需要互补支持的角色。 3 Speaking of their childhood, men recall being highly responsive to and aware of the gender-role opinions of other boys. Girls in preteen years appear to be less susceptible to gender-role pressure. It is not until the dating years that women report being concerned with feminine behavior. Males, for the most part, are responsive to the suggestion that their behavior is unmanly at almost any age. 谈到童年时,男性回忆起自己对其他男孩的性别角色观点高度敏感和在意。青春期前的女孩似乎不太容易受 到性别角色压力的影响。直到约会年龄,女性才报告开始关注女性化行为。而男性在几乎任何年龄都对暗示 其行为不够男子气概的说法做出反应。 4 These early attitudes, reinforced by social conditioning, continue to play an active part in the friendships of both sexes during adolescence. This is a period when the majority of males once again report a close alliance with same-sex friends. Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship. Although in dissimilar fashion, females share equally fragile relationships at this age. For them, the bond of loyalty extends only to the line of romantic involvement. This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence, when dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood. P1 The U.S. and China don't agree on much these days. Germany and France share a border and a currency but are frequently at odds. The U.K. and India like to march to their own drum. But there's one issue on which all these countries see eye to eye: Technology companies are too big, too powerful, and too profitable. And that power is only likely to intensify, leaving governments with no choice but to confront it head-on by taking the companies to court, passing new competition laws, and perhaps even breaking up the tech giants.

P2 China is the latest to implement an anti-trust crackdown, unveiling anti-monopoly rules last month. The draft rules followed the surprise suspension of a $37 billion stock offering by billionaire Jack Ma's Ant Group Co., making clear that no company can evade the government's regulation. The moves in China coincide with accelerating efforts in the U.S. and Europe to rein in Amazon.com, Apple, Facebook, and Google. 

P3 "The big get bigger and bigger but without being better," says Andreas Schwab, a German member of the European Parliament who championed a 2014 resolution to break up Google. "Growing economic power, growing influence on local markets all over the world, and a growing concern of competitors and consumers altogether have made it happen now."

P4 In this new anti-trust era, the old focus on pricing power no longer applies, because several of the biggest tech companies have established trillion-dollar monopolies by charging consumers next to nothing. Tech giants are increasingly assuming powerful positions in banking, finance, advertising, retail, and other markets that force smaller businesses to rely on their platforms to reach customers.

P5 For years, Europe alone confronted the power of digital giants. Governments were alarmed that European companies were failing to match Silicon Valley's innovations or to stop Google and Facebook from vacuuming up personal data and, with that, advertising revenue. Led by Margrethe Vestager, the European Union's competition chief, countries have sought to police the market and encourage fair play.

P6 In China the crackdown has been driven at least partly by fear that the homegrown tech industry is becoming too powerful. The country has long championed Alibaba and Tencent, but their massive accumulation of data on the Chinese citizenry is a growing concern for Beijing.

P7 In the U.S., a new breed of anti-trust experts argues that consideration should be given to privacy, control over data, workers' rights, and the overall impact on smaller companies. And the public in general has grown increasingly skeptical of social media companies. More than 60% say the sector has a negative effect on the country, and almost half want more regulation for social media, according to a 2020 Pew Research Center study.

P1 Born from the accessibility of mass air travel, modern international tourism has been popularized as "holiday-making" in regions that offer comparative advantages of sand, sun and sea. Travel is often portrayed as a tool for personal growth and tourism as an economic motor for destination countries and cities. There is a tendency to assume that tourism is good for everyone involved.

P2 Today the big bang of tourism drives over 1.2 billion tourists across international borders annually. Many popular places are literally being loved to death. Recent protests in ports of call like Venice and Barcelona against disturbances created by cruise ships show the unfortunate consequences of emphasizing quantity over quality in tourism.

P3 Uncontrolled tourism development has become a primary driver of social and environmental disruption. Tourism studies provide much documentation of the many negative social impacts of tourism and resulting resentment that local populations direct toward visitors.

P4 Antagonism toward tourists typically develops in mature, heavily visited destinations. Protests in heavily visited destinations suggest that traditional tourism has overstayed its welcome.

P5 Residents often become frustrated when the benefits of tourism are not felt locally. Although it can generate foreign exchange, income and employment, there's no guarantee that multinational hotel chains will allocate these benefits equitably among local communities.

P6 On the contrary, when people stay at large resorts or on cruise ships, they make most of their purchases there, leaving local communities little opportunity to benefit from tourist spending. These forms of tourism widen economic and political gaps between haves and have-nots at local destinations.

P7 In recent decades, local residents in destination communities also have found themselves negotiating new cultural boundaries, class dynamics, service industry roles and lifestyle transformations. For example, data show that tourism activity corresponds to increased social problems as local residents adopt the behaviors of tourists.

P8 What does all this mean for the everyday traveler?

P9 First, all tourists should make every effort to honor their hosts and respect local conditions. This means being prepared to adapt to local customs and norms, rather than expecting local conditions to adapt to travelers.

P10 Second, tourism is a market-based activity and works best when consumers reward better performers. In the information age, there's little excuse for travelers being uninformed about where their vacation money goes and who it enriches.

P11 Informed travelers also are better able to distinguish between multinational companies and local entrepreneurs whose businesses provide direct social, environmental, and economic benefits for local residents. Such businesses are in love with the destination and are therefore deserving of market reward. In the long run, being a responsible traveler means ensuring net positive impacts for local people and environments. With the information available at our fingertips, there has never been more opportunity to do so.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “Nowadays more and more students are becoming increasingly aware of the importance of developing digital skills.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.model: Nowadays more and more students are becoming increasingly aware of the importance of developing digital skills. This awareness is well founded, for in an age reshaped by technology, the ability to handle digital tools has become as basic as reading and writing. There are solid reasons behind this trend. For one thing, digital competence directly boosts academic efficiency. In my own case, learning to use spreadsheets and reference software turned a painful week of manual data sorting into an afternoon's work. Moreover, such skills open doors in the job market. For instance, a classmate who taught herself basic programming stood out among hundreds of applicants and landed an internship at a tech firm. As a result, students who master these tools gain a clear edge both in study and in career. In conclusion, the growing attention to digital skills reflects a genuine need rather than a passing fashion. Students would be wise to invest time in mastering practical tools instead of waiting until graduation, so that they can thrive in a world that runs on technology.

sentences.text: 春联描绘形象、抒发愿望（主语策略：原句主语） 主语 春联 Spring Festival couplets，本句有两个并列核心动词 描绘生动的形象（depict vivid images）和 抒发美好的愿望（express good wishes），共享同一主语，作两个并列谓语。

sentences.text: 手段状语前置或用介词短语 以简洁的文字 是"描绘"的方式手段，降级为介词短语 with concise words / in concise language 作方式状语，挂在谓语前后均可。主干即"春联（以简洁文字）描绘生动形象并抒发美好愿望"。

sentences.text: 单复数 生动的形象 形象不止一个，用复数 vivid images；美好的愿望 愿望不止一个，用复数 good wishes。 主谓一致 主语用复数 Spring Festival couplets，谓语 depict / express 用复数原形。 时态 回指基调用一般现在时 depict / express。
